properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 12 at 3:34PM MDT until August 12 at 4:45PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows are possible.

* WHERE...Gold Mountain burn scar in Ouray County, Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 445 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Storms producing excessive rainfall are developing
upstream and near the Gold Mountain Burn Scar. Excessive rain is
possible and could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 333 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms south of the burn scar. Flash flooding and debris
flows remain possible in Cutler and Dexter Creek drainages.
- Cutler and Dexter Creek drainages is the most likely place to
experience minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Ouray.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 12 at 3:25PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 325 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong
thunderstorms extending from 5 miles southwest of Leader to 8 miles
east of Agate, or extending from 33 miles southwest of Fort Morgan to
16 miles north of Limon, moving northeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Cottonwood Valley and Leader.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 12 at 3:24PM MDT until August 12 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Willow Burn Scar in...
Central Lake County in central Colorado...

* Until 630 PM MDT.

* At 324 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Willow Burn Scar. The expected rainfall rate is
0.5 to 1 inch in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1
inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow moving through the Rock Creek, WIllow
Creek, Rock Creek Trail and near the Leadville National Fish
Hatchery. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and
other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Willow Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Willow Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Turquoise Lake.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 12 at 1:10PM MDT until August 12 at 4:15PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central San Miguel County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 415 PM MDT.

* At 110 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain along Highway 145 from Telluride to Placerville. The
expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Placerville, Sawpit along highway 145.
